data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure only if and only if it enforces dissimilar, structurally diverse approaches across nodes (design redundancy), which often violates operators' rational economic incentive to converge on a single best-in-class stack.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Decentralized network operators intentionally adopt highly diverse stacks, libraries, and infrastructure to avoid monoculture, preserving failure independence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service's redundancy is purely structural (component-level) without design independence, meaning a single specification flaw can overcome all N redundant components simultaneously.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The external shock is so universal (e.g., a global internet outage or fundamental physics failure) that neither design diversity nor component redundancy provides protection.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independence of failure is not guaranteed by organizational decentralization; it requires design independence. Rational independent operators facing similar environments will optimize toward identical 'best-in-class' dependencies, creating a hidden monoculture. A shared external shock or a vulnerability in that shared dependency then causes synchronous degradation across the network. True resilience to correlated failure therefore requires intentional suboptimality\u2014enforcing diversity\u2014which is not the default equilibrium of a decentralized market.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
